title: [YouPass Collect] - European waste disposal methods 2005-2008
prompt: The chart below shows different methods of waste disposal in a European country from 2005 to 2008. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart illustrates the quantities of waste, measured in million tonnes, disposed of through three different methods — landfill, burning, and dumping in the sea — in a European country between 2005 and 2008.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, landfill and dumping in the sea both experienced a downward trend throughout the period, while burning followed a more fluctuating pattern. Notably, landfill was the most heavily used disposal method at the start of the period.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Starting with the two declining categories, landfill accounted for the largest share at 70 million tonnes in 2005, considerably higher than dumping in the sea, which stood at 55 million tonnes. Over the following years, landfill fell consistently by 10 million tonnes annually, ultimately reaching 40 million tonnes in 2008. Similarly, the volume of waste dumped in the sea also declined, though at a slower pace. After remaining stable at 50 million tonnes in both 2006 and 2007, it dropped to 40 million tonnes by the end of the period, matching the figure for landfill.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding burning, this method began close to landfill at 65 million tonnes in 2005 before declining steadily to its lowest point of 40 million tonnes in 2007. However, it then rebounded sharply in the final year, returning to 65 million tonnes in 2008 — the highest figure recorded across all three methods that year.
